newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Analysts cool on Generale Bank ahead of results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts cool on Generale Bank ahead of results.

text.p: Analysts were cool on shares of Generale Bank, Belgium's biggest bank, ahead of the release of its earnings after the market closes on Tuesday.
Analysts expect first-half 1996 group net profit to show a healthy rise of between eight and 18 percent.

But the share is not in favour because of speculation about a possible capital increase at the bank and the view that earnings growth will be slowed down by the consolidation of Dutch unit Generale Bank Nederland.
By 0930 GMT the share was up 100 francs or 0.89 percent at 11,325 on a firmer Brussels bourse, in line with other banks.
Early this month, a paper said Generale Bank shareholder Ste Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) was considering taking part in a capital increase at its 29.6 percent unit.
"The bank does not need the money from an operational point of view, but a capital increase would be good to improve its capital ratios," said Bank Degroof analyst Jan Longeval.
He added that based on the dividend discount model, Generale Bank shares were overvalued.
The bank has declined to comment on a possible capital increase. One analyst said maybe there would be news this afternoon, at the presentation of half-year earnings.
Brokerage Smeets, Verbaet's Ludo Colman said he had a sell recommendation on the bank, and a hold on its two competitors, Banque Bruxelles Lambert and Kredietbank.
"Kredietbank will benefit from the reweighing of the Bel-20 index (due September 20), while BBL shares still have some potential to rise on takeover speculation," he said.
He added that this would offset the effect of lower interest rate margins for the sector in the second half.

Reyers, Beauvois, Spriet analyst Philippe Koeckx also said that despite the sound full-year earnings outlook for Belgian banks, the planned partial bourse listing of publicly-owned bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) later this year would weigh on other stocks in the sector.
In the first half of 1995, Generale Bank earned a 6.73 billion franc group net profit. Estimates for the first half of 1996 ranged from 7.3 to 8.3 billion francs.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
